why: Turning {ref} moves the voltage on its middle leg anywhere between 0 V and 3.3 V, which an analog (ADC) pin can measure.

wire.ground: This puts 0 V on one outer leg of {ref}, the low end of its range.
wire.power: This puts 3.3 V on the other outer leg of {ref}, so turning the knob gives any voltage from 0 to 3.3 V.
wire.adc: {pin} is an analog input (ADC): it measures the knob's middle-leg voltage and gives the code a number from 0 to 65535.
